result.note: Tests the June 2026 FPI tax exemption on G-Secs, the Fully Accessible Route expansion and the earlier tax rates; skips the equity outflow figure as a market move.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, the Ministry of Finance exempted Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from income and capital gains taxes on Government Securities. Consider the following statements about the accompanying measures:
items: The Fully Accessible Route was expanded to include 15-, 30- and 40-year bonds alongside Sovereign Green Bonds.
The Fully Accessible Route allows non-resident investors to invest without caps.
The 'general' and 'long-term' investment categories were merged, stripping away concentration limits.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are stated in the story: the FAR, which allows uncapped non-resident investment, now covers long-dated bonds and Sovereign Green Bonds, and the two investment categories were merged. The package aims to halt capital flight and shore up a sliding rupee by attracting stickier debt capital.
questions.source: The government expanded its Fully Accessible Route (FAR) – which allows investment without caps for non-resident investors – to include 15-, 30-, and 40-year bonds alongside Sovereign Green Bonds.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the taxes FPIs faced in India before the June 2026 exemption on Government Securities:
items: Long-term capital gains tax on listed shares and bonds — 12.5%
Holding period to qualify as long-term — More than 24 months
Withholding tax on interest from government bonds — 20%
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The long-term holding period was more than 12 months, not 24 months; the 12.5% and 20% rates are correctly matched. The complete waiver on Government Securities aims to align India with competing global bond markets.
questions.source: FPIs previously faced 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on listed ​shares and bonds held for more than ​12 months, ⁠and a 20% withholding tax on interest earned from government bonds.
